support.title: Support Natively
support.body: Natively is built and maintained by one developer. If it's part of your daily workflow, your support keeps it moving forward.

about.title: About Natively
about.tagline: Designed to be invisible, intelligent, and trusted.
about.zhBuildNotice: This is a community Simplified Chinese build. It never downloads or installs official updates automatically. Installing an official release will replace this build and remove the Chinese interface.

news.uiStylesBody: Introduced two gorgeous, immersive interface themes, Liquid Glass and Modern Dark, to completely redefine your real-time overlay experience.
news.deepseekBody: Full support for DeepSeek's advanced reasoning models, delivering ultra-smart and cost-effective chat replies.
news.audioBody: Hardened macOS system audio process tapping and security permission gates to guarantee robust capture streams.
news.modesBody: The Profile Intelligence matrix and Modes Manager have been optimized like crazy for responsive, ultra-low latency context processing.
news.updatesBody: Enjoy seamless, single-click updates directly inside the desktop app with zero manual installation loops.

how.hybridBody: Seamlessly routes queries between ultra-fast models for instant speed and reasoning models (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude) for complex tasks. Powered by enterprise-grade speech recognition from 7+ providers.

privacy.stealthBody: Features "Undetectable Mode" to hide from the dock and "Masquerading" to disguise as system apps. You control exactly what data leaves your device.
privacy.noRecordingBody: Natively listens only when active. It does not record video, take arbitrary screenshots without command, or perform background surveillance.

about.creatorQuote1: I build software that stays out of the way.
about.creatorQuote2: <0></0> is made to feel fast, quiet, and respectful of your privacy.

support.starBody: Love Natively? Support us by starring the repo.
support.issueBody: Found a bug? Let us know so we can fix it.
support.contactBody: Open for professional collaborations and job offers.

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.subtitle: Get Natively running in four steps.
quickStart.step1Mac: Enable Screen Recording and Accessibility for Natively in macOS Privacy & Security.
quickStart.step1Win: Approve the microphone prompt the first time you start a meeting (Settings → Privacy → Microphone).
quickStart.step2Desc: Open Settings → Audio and select Natively API, or paste a Deepgram or Google key.
quickStart.step3Desc: Open Settings → AI Providers and choose a built-in model, or add a Groq or OpenRouter key.
quickStart.step4Desc: Drop your resume + JD in Profile Intelligence, link your Google Calendar, or pick a Mode tailored to your session.

page.title: Help & Setup Guide
page.subtitle: Learn how to deeply configure Natively. Everything from providing the right API scopes to executing conversational interviews seamlessly is covered below.
page.skipSetupTitle: Want to skip the manual setup?
page.skipSetupBody: Use the <0></0> for an out-of-the-box experience. One-click zero-configuration usage.

guide.s1IntroMac: Natively operates entirely on-device, but requires OS permissions to tap into your screen context and global keystrokes. Here is how your system should look:
guide.s1IntroWin: Natively operates entirely on-device. Windows will prompt you for microphone access the first time you start a meeting — no other OS permissions are required.
guide.loopbackDesc: Natively can capture both what you say and what you hear globally. At the top of the Audio Settings, use the Dropdowns to explicitly select your hardware Input (e.g. your physical microphone) and Output capture (what the speakers play). By default, Natively utilizes the <0></0>, so audio routing will automatically follow your OS preferences.
guide.sckDesc: The recommended backend for macOS 13.0+. Uses Apple's modern, highly optimized internal framework for 0-latency loopback speaker capture securely.
guide.coreAudioDesc: Fallback engine for older hardware. Relies on internal device aggregation to trap output audio. Only use this if SCK repeatedly drops speaker packets.
guide.languageDesc: Below the provider list, you must specify the <0></0> you will be speaking (e.g., English). Most importantly, ensure you select your specific regional <1></1> mapping (e.g., <2></2> vs <3></3> vs <4></4>) as STT backends use this map to vastly increase transcription accuracy logic based on regional inflections.
guide.permScreenDesc: Provides Natively the ability to read your screen temporarily when you capture context.
guide.pathMacScreen: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording
guide.permAccessibilityDesc: Required for Natively to detect the global keyboard shortcuts below, regardless of what window is focused.
guide.permMicDesc: Required to capture what you say during meetings. Windows prompts the first time you start a meeting.
guide.sttIntro: Natively supports over 8 different Audio engines to transcribe what you hear and say. From the Audio tab in settings, use the overarching dropdown to switch the active engine.
guide.apiKeysDesc: We strongly recommend testing connections before jumping into a live meeting. The system shows successful pings or explicit errors if credits/permissions fail.
guide.p1Desc: Uses a Service Account JSON instead of an API Key. You must build a GCP Project, activate the Cloud Speech API, and create a Service Account under IAM. Download the JSON Key, and drag-and-drop it into the box in the Audio Settings.
guide.p2Desc: When creating a Custom API key for the "Conversational AI" streaming integration, you must explicitly enable <0></0> and <1></1>. Crucially, you must also allow <2></2> as seen below in the ElevenLabs UI:
guide.p2Tail: as seen below in the ElevenLabs UI:
guide.p3Desc: Provides ultra-fast Whisper responses via LPUs. Starts with <0></0>. No special permissions required.
guide.p4Desc: Uses standard OpenAI keys (<0></0>). Remember: this Audio key is isolated from your AI Generation key under "AI Providers".
guide.p5Desc: Extremely accurate streaming transcription (Nova-2 model). Key is generated on-demand in the Deepgram Console.
guide.p6Desc: Requires establishing Azure Speech Services. <0></0>: You must also specify an Azure Region alongside your key (e.g. <1></1>, <2></2>) or requests will bounce.
guide.p7Desc: Create a Watson Speech to Text resource in IBM Cloud and generate a set of API credentials.
guide.p8Desc: Provides high-end medical/law tier transcriptions using their standard dashboard API Key.
guide.llmIntro: Natively uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to reason about your screen and audio context. You can configure cloud providers, local models, or fully custom endpoints.
guide.llmGroqDesc: Ultra-fast inference using LPU hardware. Default model: <0></0>.
guide.registrySyncDesc: <0></0> Natively utilizes a 14-day background sync clock (<1></1>) to silently poll upstream APIs. If Anthropic or OpenAI drops a new flagship architecture (e.g. GPT-5), your app dynamically absorbs it into the UI dropdown automatically.
guide.activeModelDesc: Inside the Launcher UI (above the start button), you can hot-swap your <0></0>. This dictation is extremely important—it determines the active core reasoning engine. If set to <1></1>, the intelligence agent uses Anthropic infrastructure exclusively for screen analysis. Switch to <2></2> beneath it, and the architecture instantly reverts to generating responses via your offline GPU pipeline.
guide.ollamaStep2: Open Terminal and run our recommended 8B parameter instruction model:
guide.ollamaStep3: Alternatively, for faster generation without GPU, use Microsoft's smaller model:
guide.ollamaStep4: Return to Natively's AI Providers overlay, and you will see your Local models ready for usage.
guide.customProvidersDesc: Use Custom Providers to hook up any standard external LLM router (like OpenRouter, LMStudio, or proprietary company endpoints). Create a new provider using a cURL command template.
guide.responsePathDesc: <0></0> You must inform Natively how to parse the JSON text back. Deeply nested outputs must define the exact path array. For OpenAI/OpenRouter compliant endpoints, this is strictly: <1></1>.
guide.interfaceIntro: When initialized, Natively hides itself visually while remaining active as a persistent translucent overlay. This is your command center.
guide.qaWhatToAnswerDesc: Reads the active transcript and screen, then streams a precise response to read aloud.
guide.qaBrainstormDesc: Recap becomes Brainstorm when Interview Mode is ON — deep multi-step strategies.
guide.qaFollowUpDesc: Suggests the next logical question to keep conversation flowing gracefully.
guide.qaAnswerNowDesc: Records your mic + screen context and fires an immediate AI query.
guide.qaClarifyDesc: Generates sharp probing questions from latent audio when a topic is unclear.
guide.qaRecapDesc: Condenses the last 5 minutes into bullet points when you lose the thread.
guide.qaCodeHintDesc: Reads your screen and nudges you toward the correct code implementation.
guide.qaScreenshotAskDesc: Forces a full-screen capture and immediately processes it through the LLM.
guide.qaStealthDesc: Processes context in the background without ever revealing the interface.
guide.meetingIntelIntro: When an active session concludes, it gets saved directly to your local file system as a complete intelligence dossier spanning the transcript, AI token usage, and automated structural summaries.
guide.summaryDesc: Natively fires a local background job as soon as the meeting finishes to compress the entire raw audio transcript into clean, formatted markdown representing structural overviews and explicit action items.
guide.rawTranscriptDesc: Dive into the exact dialogue timeline. Speaker separation attempts to classify "Me" vs "Them" using volume thresholds, capturing everything physically said alongside timestamps.
guide.usageDesc: View exactly how many tokens the AI consumed globally across the meeting, tracking visual and textual inputs separately.
guide.semanticSearchDesc: Instead of re-reading the entire transcript to find what happened, use the attached RAG interface pinned to the bottom of the Meeting details window.
guide.contextualSearchDesc: You don't need to craft long AI prompts. Simply ask, "What API dependencies did they list?" and the system injects the localized transcript from that specific timeline to provide highly-accurate responses dynamically.
guide.memoryIsolationDesc: Conversations here are strictly isolated to the selected meeting boundaries. They do not utilize global memory, ensuring hyper-focused extraction without cross-contamination.
guide.globalPaletteDesc: Hit <0></0> anywhere on your computer to invoke the Natively Global Palette. This acts as your Spotlight overlay for interacting directly with the system backbone.
guide.traversalDesc: Typing any text instantly fuzzy matches across all your previous meeting titles, summaries, and internal files. Hitting enter jumps you straight into the intelligence viewer for that topic.
guide.fallbackDesc: If your query doesn't match an existing document, the palette offers a direct jump to spark off a standard LLM chat conversation passing through your exact typed intent.
guide.globalShortcutsDesc: These hotkeys work anywhere on your operating system, regardless of whether Natively is focused or completely hidden. Change them via <0></0>.
guide.scToggleDesc: Quickly toggle the window visibility. Used as an immediate panic hide.
guide.scCaptureDesc: Takes a silent screenshot in the background, feeding the visual data to the LLM context flow.
guide.scProcessDesc: Triggers Natively to analyze the captured screenshots and text from the rolling buffer.
guide.scBothDesc: Captures a screenshot AND processes it in one fluid action.
guide.profileDesc: Instead of telling the AI who you are during every prompt, Profile Intelligence parses your background and universally injects it into all queries so it responds securely customized to your job role.
guide.benefit1: Model inherits your coding stack, experience, etc.
guide.benefit2: Upload your PDF Resume for local extraction.
guide.proRequirementDesc: This is a Natively Pro feature.
guide.dropResume: Drop your Resume PDF in the UI to activate injection.
guide.jdTargetingDesc: Drop a target <0></0> alongside your resume. Natively extracts the role title, level, company, and required technologies, then biases every prompt to align your responses with that exact spec — perfect for staying on-message during a final loop.
guide.companyIntelDesc: After uploading a JD, hit <0></0> to compile a live dossier on the company — recent news, product surface area, culture signals — cached and injected into every reply so you sound briefed without prep.
guide.negotiationDesc: Generate a <0></0> calibrated against the active JD's level and your background. Live coaching shows up inline during compensation conversations.
guide.customContextDesc: In addition to your Resume and JD, type any free-form context into the <0></0> textarea — sales stats, product details, LeetCode solutions, personal preferences. Injected as a <1></1> block into every AI call, across all modes and providers.
guide.customContextStep4: Up to 4,000 characters with a live counter
guide.putItem1: Your company's product details or pricing
guide.modesIntro: Modes let you assign a specialized AI persona to your session. Each mode has a tailored system prompt, a personal context area, reference files, and smart note template sections — so Natively behaves differently depending on whether you're in a sales call, a coding interview, or a team standup.
guide.modeDesc1: STAR-format answers, behavioral stories, step-by-step coding hints.
guide.modeDesc2: Objection handling, discovery questions, product pitch frameworks.
guide.modeDesc3: Candidate assessment, JD cross-referencing, structured evaluation.
guide.modeDesc4: Action items, announcements, blockers, decisions — auto-extracted.
guide.modeDesc5: Concept breakdowns, intuition-first explanations, formula notes.
guide.modeDesc6: DSA / system design reasoning, edge cases, complexity analysis.
guide.modesOpenStep1: Click the <0></0> in the Launcher header
guide.modesOpenStep2: Or click the grid icon in the main interface toolbar
guide.modesActivateStep1: Select any mode in the left sidebar
guide.modesActivateStep3: The toolbar icon shows the active mode name live
guide.refStep1: Upload PDF, DOCX, or TXT files per mode
guide.refStep2: File contents are injected as real-time context
guide.refStep3: Great for: resumes, product sheets, job descriptions
guide.refStep4: Per-file cap: 12 k chars · total cap: 40 k chars
guide.modesProGate: Modes are locked behind Natively Pro. Free and trial users see only the General mode. Activate a license via <0></0> to unlock all seven modes.
guide.calendarDesc: By connecting your Google Calendar directly to Natively, the AI automatically gains context on your upcoming meetings, syncs the event data, and reads attendee lists to hyper-personalize your interactions.
guide.calendarStep3: Natively will quietly background-sync your schedule.
guide.followUpDesc: When tracking live meetings, Natively uses the connected calendar context to instantly figure out <0></0>. This powers the Follow-Up Email system, letting you auto-draft post-meeting notes to confirmed attendees.
guide.peekStackDesc: The Launcher's Calendar card now displays your <0></0> with a stacked-card visual hinting at what comes after it — no need to switch tabs to see what's queued.
guide.oneClickJoinDesc: Each upcoming event shows a <0></0> button that opens the meeting link in your <1></1> (so it lands in the right Chrome/Safari profile), not an in-app webview.
guide.fastModeDesc: Fast Mode activates highly efficient models (like Llama 3 8B) layered over Groq hardware LPUs instead of GPUs. This brings latency down from 2-3 seconds to less than 500ms. To enable Fast Mode, navigate to Settings > General Settings popup overlay, and click the Lightning Icon.
guide.phoneMirrorDesc: Phone Mirror spins up a small local web server so you can watch Natively's live transcript and AI answers from your phone or tablet — handy when your screen is being shared and you don't want the overlay visible.
guide.phoneMirrorStep2: Toggle on, then scan the generated QR code from your phone
guide.phoneMirrorStep3: Loopback by default — flip <0></0> to reach it from another device on the same Wi-Fi
guide.phoneMirrorSecurityDesc: Every session is protected by a single-use bearer token baked into the QR. If a device leaves your trust circle, hit <0></0> to invalidate every existing connection in one tap.
guide.lanExposureWarning: <0></0> Only enable <1></1> on networks you trust. The token stops casual snoops, but anyone who captures the QR or copies the URL can read your live transcript until you rotate.
guide.stealthDesc: Natively is heavily geared towards power users seeking minimalistic operation. The process completely disguises itself and remains undetectable/invisible to standard screen-recording applications and desktop sharing utilities.
guide.opacityDesc: Decrease your visual footprint to near-zero. Navigate to the General Settings overlay and dynamically drag the <0></0> down to make the interface completely translucent against your underlying native applications.
guide.passthroughDesc: Do you want the AI prompt completely fused into your screen without obstructing your clicks? Activate <0></0> inside the UI toggle menu.
guide.passthroughWarning: <0></0> This renders the Natively overlay completely unclickable. You MUST memorize the Global Hotkeys (e.g. <1></1> to move, <2></2> to hide, <3></3> for actions) to control the application once this is active.
